I don't know why I bought this game. I'm not particularly into the retro 8-bit look that's so prevalent. I'm not quite big on platformers and my reflexes have atrophied since my Super Mario (dare I say even Pitfall?) days. But I do like a good "rogue-like" (read: life is cheap and the world is procedurally-generated) and it was embarrasingly cheap, so I gave it a shot. 

And I keep going back to it so much more than the bigger, more expensive games I bought. Plenty of powerups, stackable, with more carrot than stick: it rewards you more than it punishes you. Or [b]before[/b] it punishes you.  You'll die many times before you find the teleporter.  You'll die many times before your 90 seconds is up.  You'll die many times at the hands/pincers/tentacles/plasma of the first boss.  And the ease of restarting and reattacking the game keeps bringing you back.

It's very engrossing, one of those "just one more try" games that manages to be big without being mind-numbingly epic (in a daunting way).  It's my biggest surprise in the Steam store.

This game really surprised me. I heard good things from other people, but it kept off my radar for quite a long time. I didn't touch it, hear much about it until later on, and felt like I could do without it.

But then I decided just to buy it on a whim.

I've easily fallen in love with the game. I've never liked games that make you die. That make sure you die. That tries it's damnest just to maim, torture, and kill you. But this game does it -right-

The whole basis of the game is less on that though, and more on the actual journey. The stage-by-stage dynamic in which you have to find a teleporter, and go to the next stage. It's all designed around this aspect. How do I mean?

There's a timer. The longer the timer goes, the harder it gets. So you must go through as fast as possible. But it can't be -that- simple, right? No. Of course not. The game's tender love and care is equal to that of an insane Buffalo Bill enjoying your flesh from above the hole. You have to get items in order to help you through the game. Enemies can drop them, but enemies will mostly give you money, and if you have enough, you can purchase them whilst running around the area.

So that's where the problem lies. Do you stay, farm enough for some more items for the challenge ahead? Or go through as fast as possible to keep the difficulty down? That's why it's so fun. This simple form expanded upon by the smallest things change the game entirely. What items you end up getting. How much time you have. What character you use to help you get through. And how much behind it all is included as well. From character unlocks, to different items the more challenges you do.

And that's what makes it great.

Not to mention the kickass design, and the beautiful atmospheric music. I couldn't help myself but actually -buy- the soundtrack on iTunes. I haven't heard a soundtrack this... Comfy. This beautiful in a certain way since Metroid Prime. The graphics are exactly how they need to be. Minimalist. It doesn't seem like it's pixel-art for the sake of "muh nostalgia" but for the sake of actually being how it should be. The artistic view of how the game should look and feel.

And that's why I love it. This game is definitely recommended.

I haven't played too much of this game only 6 games of it but There are both pros and cons.
Pros
-addicting gameplay
-responsive controls
-fun action rpg gameplay
-good item bonus system
-good soundtrack
-fun with or without friends
cons
-enemy spawn rate is too high
-enemys give you little to no time to heal
-enemies jump in during boss fights
-Only 1 class to choose from at first
-no tutorial just drops you right into the gameplay(this could either be a pro or con)
In conclusion this game with both pros and cons is still a good game
